title: Geometric unipotence gives a unitriangular closed embedding over the base field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$. Suppose there exist $m\geq1$ and a homomorphism $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] such that $\rho(R)$ is injective for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, and such that for every $g\in G(\bar k)$ the matrix $\rho(g)$ is unipotent: $(\rho(g)-I_m)^N=0$ for some integer $N\geq1$. Here $\bar k$ is an algebraic closure of $k$, and $G(R)$ means the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}R\to G$ over $k$. Then for some $n\geq1$ there is a homomorphism $i:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ that is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and factors through the upper unitriangular closed subgroup scheme $\mathcal U_n$. Explicitly, $\mathcal U_n(R)$ consists of matrices $(a_{ij})$ with $a_{ii}=1$ and $a_{ij}=0$ for $i>j$, with matrix multiplication; it is represented by the polynomial algebra $k[x_{ij}:1\leq i<j\leq n]$. The factor $G\to\mathcal U_n$ is a closed immersion over $k$, not merely after field extension. No perfectness or connectedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 14.12, printed p.283, and Theorem 14.5(a)⇒(b), printed pp.281–282; Corollary 3.35, printed p.75, for faithfulness as trivial scheme-theoretic kernel.

proof.text: Set $V=k^m$ and $K=\bar k$. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-faithful-closed-immersion] to $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$. Both groups are affine of finite type, the target by its presentation $k[x_{ij},D^{-1}]/(D D^{-1}-1)$ in [def-sc-general-linear-group]; injectivity for every commutative $k$-algebra is exactly the hypothesis of the item. Thus $\rho$ is a closed immersion over $k$. We will construct a basis of this same $V$ making $\rho$ unitriangular; no new faithful representation is required.

source.place: Corollary 3.35, printed p.75; the faithful representation in Theorem 14.5(a)⇒(b), printed p.281.

proof.text: Construct a flag by induction. Suppose $0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_r\subseteq V$ consists of $k$-subspaces with $\dim F_j=j$ and $g e_j-e_j\in R\otimes_k F_{j-1}$ for every $R$, every $g\in G(R)$, and chosen basis vectors $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $F_r$. Initially $r=0$. If $r<m$, put $W=V/F_r$, of dimension $d=m-r>0$. This is a rational $G$-representation: extend $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ to a $k$-basis of $V$; the lower-left block of the action matrix is zero for every $R$, so its lower-right block acts on $R\otimes_k W$, is invertible (apply the same to $g^{-1}$), and respects multiplication and change of $R$. For $g\in G(K)$ the equality $(\rho(g)-I)^N=0$ descends to $(g_W-I)^N=0$ on $K\otimes_k W$, by applying the quotient map to that equality.

source.place: Corollary 14.2, printed p.280, inductive quotient construction; Proposition 14.3, same page, invariant flags.

proof.text: The image $H$ of $G(K)$ acting on $K\otimes_k W$ is a subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_d(K)$ after choosing a basis of $W$: products and inverses are images of products and inverses in $G(K)$. Every element of $H$ is unipotent by step 2. Since $d>0$, [lem-sfb-unipotent-matrix-group-fixed-vector] gives a nonzero vector fixed by all of $H$, hence by all of $G(K)$. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-invariant-descent] to this rational $G$-action on $W$. The field, smoothness, affineness and finite-type hypotheses are precisely those on $G$ in the item. Its comparison identifies the pointwise fixed subspace with $K\otimes_k W^G$ and asserts $W^G\ne0$. Choose $0\ne w\in W^G$ over $k$, and lift it to $e_{r+1}\in V$.

source.place: Proposition 14.1 and Corollary 14.2, printed pp.279--280; Corollary 4.34, printed p.97, and the descent step of Corollary 14.9, printed p.282.

proof.text: Put $F_{r+1}=F_r+k e_{r+1}$. Since the image $w$ of $e_{r+1}$ in $W$ is nonzero, $\dim F_{r+1}=r+1$. For every $R$ and $g\in G(R)$, invariance of $w$ says that $g e_{r+1}-e_{r+1}$ lies in the kernel of $R\otimes_k V\to R\otimes_k W$, which is $R\otimes_k F_r$: in the chosen basis this map simply discards the first $r$ coordinates. Thus the induction hypotheses hold for $r+1$. Each iteration increases $r$ by one, and at $r=m$ the vectors $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ form a $k$-basis of $V$. In this basis all action matrices have diagonal entries $1$ and entries below the diagonal $0$, for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$.

source.place: Corollary 14.2, printed p.280, continued to a full basis; Proposition 14.3, same page.

proof.text: Let $P\in\operatorname{GL}_m(k)$ have columns $e_j$, and set $i(g)=P^{-1}\rho(g)P$. Conjugation and its inverse are morphisms over $k$, since their entries are linear combinations of matrix entries and their determinants equal the original determinant. Hence $i$ is a homomorphism and a closed immersion: on coordinate algebras its map is the surjection $\rho^*$ precomposed with the conjugation automorphism. Write $A=k[x_{ij},D^{-1}]$ and let $J$ be generated by $x_{ii}-1$ and the $x_{ij}$ for $i>j$. In $A/J$ the determinant is $1$, so $A/J=k[x_{ij}:i<j]$. These equations define $\mathcal U_m$. They are preserved by products and inverses: for strictly upper triangular $T$, $T^m=0$ (a nonzero product requires a strictly increasing chain of indices), and $(I+T)^{-1}=\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}(-T)^s$. By step 4 the equations vanish on $i_R(g)$ for every $R,g$; in particular take $R=k[G]$ and the universal point $\operatorname{id}_{k[G]}$ to get $i^*(J)=0$. The induced map $A/J\to k[G]$ is still surjective, since $A\to k[G]$ is. By the affine criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion], this gives a closed immersion $G\to\mathcal U_m$ whose composite into $\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ is $i$. Take $n=m\geq1$. The construction, including its defining surjection, is over $k$.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(a)⇒(b), printed p.281; coordinate presentation of U_n on the same page, with the explicit affine factorization written out.

lean.statement: theorem geometric_unipotence_unitriangular_embedding {k : Type u} [Field k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [IsAffine G.left] [Smooth G.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (rho : G ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (ULift.{u} (Fin m)) k) [IsMonHom rho] (hinj : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R], Function.Injective (fun x : (Spec (.of R)).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ G ↦ x ≫ rho)) (hunip : ∀ x : (Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure k))).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ⟶ G, ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ ((GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (ULift.{u} (Fin m)) k (AlgebraicClosure k) (x ≫ rho)).val - 1) ^ N = 0) : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∃ (U : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (f : G ⟶ U.X) (j : U.X ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) k), IsMonHom f ∧ IsMonHom j ∧ IsClosedImmersion f.left ∧ IsClosedImmersion j.left ∧ IsClosedImmersion (f ≫ j).left ∧ ∃ e : U.X ≅ (Spec (.of (MvPolynomial {p : Fin n × Fin n // p.1 < p.2} k))).asOver (Spec (.of k)), ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (phi : MvPolynomial {p : Fin n × Fin n // p.1 < p.2} k →ₐ[k] R) (a b : Fin n), (GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) k R ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom phi.toRingHom)).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ≫ e.inv ≫ j)).val (ULift.up a) (ULift.up b) = if h : a < b then phi (MvPolynomial.X ⟨(a, b), h⟩) else if a = b then 1 else 0
